critique:
field blue_deposited, POLICY PROMPT
  For the three-blue, two-green goal, the first blue cube was carried to an elevated release pose, the fingers opened, and the empty hand withdrew. The policy retained zero although the completed-deposit count was one. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure, not a need for additional memory. Retain the cumulative integer field and its existing update rule, but make explicit that a tracked held cube followed by release at the bin-release pose and empty withdrawal is positive deposit evidence. Independently visible free cubes, including a nearby same-color cube that persists through the interval, do not contradict it. Only continuity showing the carried cube itself released or falling outside the bin defeats that evidence; neither wrist-to-bin-center coordinate mismatch nor failure of total visible count to decrease does so. Initialize to zero and increment once per completed blue deposit observed in the supplied interval, giving, for example, 1 after the first release. Do not increment for pickup or issuing B.

field red_deposited, POLICY PROMPT
  For a two-red goal, the first carried red cube was released at the elevated bin-release pose and the empty hand withdrew, while other red cubes remained or appeared. The policy retained zero and selected another cube, although the completed-deposit count was one. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure. Retain the cumulative integer field, but emphasize that held-cube continuity, opening fingers at the bin-release pose, and empty withdrawal establish a deposit unless the interval positively tracks that carried cube outside the bin. Newly appearing or persistent free cubes are not such evidence, and elevated wrist coordinates need not coincide with the visible bin center. Initialize to zero; increment once at the decision following each observed completed red deposit, for example to 1 after the first deposit, and preserve through pickups, retries, and unrelated cube appearances.

field green_deposited, POLICY PROMPT
  For the one-blue, two-green goal with the bin near [109, 100], a held green cube reached the elevated release pose, fingers opened near [62, 88], and the empty hand withdrew. Other green cubes remained visible. The policy kept zero and chose blue, whereas the completed green-deposit count was one. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure. Retain the cumulative integer field and clarify the existing release-evidence rule: the elevated release pose may project well above and to either side of the bin center. Held-cube continuity followed by opening and empty withdrawal establishes completion without directly seeing entry into the opaque bin. Other free green cubes do not establish an outside release; that exception requires evidence tracking the carried cube itself outside the bin. Initialize to zero and increment once per observed completed green deposit, for example to 1 after this first release; preserve otherwise.

the policy prompt for subgoal
  For the three-blue, two-green goal in the layout with the bin near [112, 161], the policy repeatedly used the smallest-y fallback to select green when the recorded choices required three blue pickups first, and then selected the wrong green cubes. For two-red and three-red goals, fallback or unsupported selection likewise picked an available but different red cube after a deposit. For the one-blue, two-green goal with the bin near [109, 100], fallback selected blue too early and later selected the wrong blue cube. The relevant completed-deposit counts were recoverable from incoming counters and the observed releases; no new historical target or phase field is required. These are SUFFICIENCY failures of the target-selection rules, alongside the separate deposit-update failures. Preserve existing preferences and the quota/held-cube rules, but add the following goal-and-layout-conditioned preferences ahead of fallback. For three blue and two green with the bin near [112, 161], complete blue before green: select blue near [66, 141], [81, 71], and [94, 131] when the updated blue_deposited count is respectively zero, one, and two; once three blue deposits are complete, select green near [78, 109] and [72, 172] when green_deposited is respectively zero and one. For two red with the bin near [118, 175], select red near [105, 118] at count zero and [60, 163] at count one. For two red with the bin near [95, 162], select red near [53, 80] at count zero and [77, 139] at count one, rather than the newly visible red near [74, 161]. For three red with the bin near [109, 112], select red near [113, 142], [70, 82], and [95, 158] at counts zero, one, and two; distinguish this from the existing three-red layout near [110, 130] using the visible arrangement as well as the bin. For one blue and two green with the bin near [109, 100], complete green before blue: select green near [108, 152] at green count zero and [75, 88] at count one, then blue near [117, 71] after two green deposits while blue count is zero. Match these approximate anchors to current free cubes using the current scene and supplied interval, not remembered initial observations or exact pixel equality. Apply preferences only with an empty hand and unmet quotas, after updating counters; a currently held requested cube still calls for B, and satisfied quotas call for C despite remaining free cubes. Use fallback only when no applicable preference selects an available candidate. No existing preference or general transition rule needs deletion.
